title: VeloHealth - Stability Bridgecall: Ownership Playbook
summary: Bridge call to align on post-incident responsibilities after the 2026-02-16 degradation. Agreed owners for timeline, repro bench, KV cache replay, and short/medium term mitigations. Action items and a pilot for staggered route fallbacks were planned.
next_steps: Alex to send annotated incident timeline and logs link by 2026-02-21
Priya to run KV-cache replay on staging and share results by 2026-02-23

transcript:
Meeting header:
Date/Time: 2026-02-19 15:00 UTC
Duration: 52 minutes
Attendees: Alex Thompson (Redwood AE), Priya Kapoor (Redwood SE), Maya Lin (VeloHealth Head of Platform), Jordan O'Neal (VeloHealth SRE), Samir Patel (VeloHealth CTO)
Links shared: Incident timeline (in progress) https://redwood.app/notes/velo-esc-88942 , quick slide w/ fallback options https://redwood.app/slides/fallbacks-2026

[00:00] Alex: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, we'll kick off in a sec. I can see Maya, Jordan and Samir joined — thanks for making time. The goal is to leave with owners for the short term mitigations and a clear next check-in.

[00:22] Maya: Yeah thanks Alex. Um, we had a pretty rough Friday, so appreciate the follow-up. We want the action items, like what to do now vs what we do in the medium term.

[00:34] Priya: Quick note — I'll be the SE lead on the reproductions and the KV cache replay. Alex will handle the timeline + ops comms. We'll need the trace bundle from your end, Jordan.

[00:46] Jordan: Right, I'll get that. There's some PII in the traces so Samir, we need clearance to share a redacted set.

[00:55] Samir: We can do redacted. We'll work with security to get a short window of access.

[01:05] Alex: Cool. For context, the incident looked like a tail-latency surge tied to a hot path — the K-V cash (laugh) sorry, KV cache — eviction pattern we hadn't seen at that scale. Priya, feel free to correct me if I'm butchering the details.

[01:20] Priya: No you're close. The hot path was the streaming token write into KV; we saw a combination of big sequence lengths and small batch size leading to frequent cache thrash. Also a fallback routing loop made it worse — some requests re-tried into the same overloaded pool.

[01:38] Maya: Sorry, re-tried into same pool, is that because of sticky routing? I thought routing is region+model.

[01:46] Priya: Good question. It's policy-based — by default it's region then tier. But when a node evicted the prefix cache, the orchestration retried to the last-used worker because it still had a partial KV handle; that produced hot replays. The routing fallback policy is recent and not fully instrumented in your account.

[02:10] Jordan: That matches our logs — we saw a wall of retries for the same session IDs. Our SLOs were breached for about 18 minutes.

[02:20] Alex: Ok so immediate goals: 1) contain and stop retry loops, 2) reproduce and measure, 3) short-term circuit/fallback, 4) medium-term config and dedicated sizing. Does that list match?

[02:31] Maya: Yes. Also we need to own comms — what we tell product/execs.

[02:36] Alex: We'll produce the incident timeline with high level note for execs plus the annotated trace for eng.

[02:42] Priya: For reproductions, I'm proposing we do a KV-cache replay test in staging which will rehydrate a similar prefix distribution, then run a continuous token gen workload at the same qps distribution. We'll capture tail-latency CDFs and per-worker heatmaps.

[03:00] Jordan: Can you do that with our dataset? We have concerns about redaction and also about the token lengths — can you parameterize the replay?

[03:08] Priya: Yep. We can parameterize sequence length, batch size and the prefix skew. We don't need unredacted PII for performance testing; hashed session IDs work fine.

[03:20] Samir: Walk me through the short term fallback you mentioned earlier. Is that a routing change or a code patch?

[03:28] Alex: Short term we'd flip the retry policy to not prefer last-used worker and add a brief jitter + global per-session retry cap. That's a config change and safe to deploy quickly.

[03:38] Priya: Additionally, we can add a temporary canary that routes heavy sequence length requests to a larger instance profile — think faster kernels with higher kv cache capacity — as a stop-gap. It's a policy change in the console, no code.

[03:53] Maya: That sounds promising. What's the expected cost delta? Execs will ask.

[03:58] Priya: Rough ballpark — if you move 10% of traffic to the larger profile it might be around a 5-7% increase in monthly inference spend for that window. We'll produce a cost estimate.

[04:12] Jordan: And for Dedicated — if we go that route — we'll need committed sizing. Samir, is there appetite to pilot dedicated for this hot path?

[04:20] Samir: Potentially. But we need numbers. If the pilot reduces tail by 80% for the critical flows, it might be worth it. Also security asks about data residency for some workloads.

[04:33] Alex: That's on the medium-term list: Dedicated pilot sizing, expected QPS, and residency requirements. We'll treat it as a separate proposal.

[04:40] Maya: Can we talk SLIs? We had the SLO thresholds but the incident page didn't make it clear which request types hit the breach.

[04:47] Jordan: Mostly streaming responses with long contexts — sessions > 1024 tokens.

[04:52] Priya: Ok, so param for the replay: sequence_length > 1024, skewed prefix reuse, 60% small batch sizes, intermittent cold starts. We'll capture p95,p99,p999.

[05:10] Alex: Great. Now I want to call out instrumentation gaps — we noted the fallback policy wasn't fully surfaced in your account metrics. We'll share an instrumentation checklist so you can turn on per-route retry and per-worker eviction metrics.

[05:24] Maya: That checklist will be super helpful. Please make it prescriptive — config paths, required flags, where to look in the console.

[05:31] Alex: Will do. We'll link to a playbook with exact UI steps.

[05:36] Priya: There's one more technical deep point — the KV eviction pattern seemed correlated with quantized kernel memory pressure on the machine. We're seeing more thrash when mixed model sizes are colocated. For the medium term, we recommend profiling and either pinning heavy models to separate pools or enforcing isolation.

[05:58] Jordan: Pinning heavy models — ok. How invasive is that?

[06:02] Priya: It's mostly a deployment and autoscale policy change. It might require capacity to be reserved which is why Dedicated or reserved pools help.

[06:10] Samir: If we reserve, what's the timeline to get a small Dedicated pool?

[06:15] Alex: For a pilot it's usually 2-3 weeks to provision and baseline, maybe faster if you accept a smaller initial commit. We'll draft a pilot proposal.

[06:24] Maya: I want to flag audits — our security team will ask for full audit logs around the incident. What level of logs can you provide?

[06:31] Alex: We can provide request-level traces, route-level decision logs, and orchestration events. For Private/VPC there's an option to keep logs in your KMS, but for hosted we provide redacted export. We'll include the ask in the timeline doc.

[06:46] Jordan: Also, one operational ask — can you add a rate-limiter rule for sessions that exceed X tokens to avoid single-session storms?

[06:53] Priya: That's doable as a per-route throttling rule. We can add an adaptive throttle that kicks in when a session's per-minute token consumption exceeds a threshold.

[07:03] Samir: We should be careful — throttling could cause user-visible errors. We want graceful degradation, not hard failures.

[07:09] Maya: Right, graceful degrade + clear monitoring so product knows when degradation is active.

[07:15] Alex: Ok we'll include policy for graceful degrade: prefer function-level fallback -> model variant -> dedicated route. The playbook will list exact fallbacks and user-facing messaging.

[07:26] Priya: Quick note on benchmarking — we'll produce CDF plots, per-worker heatmaps, and a small script you can run in your environment to reproduce.

[07:36] Jordan: If you can give us the script, we can iterate faster.

[07:40] Priya: Absolutely, script + runbook.

[07:44] Alex: Let's assign owners (voice): Alex — timeline + exec note; Priya — replay + bench script; Jordan — provide redacted traces and thresholds; Samir/Maya — decide on Dedicated interest and gather security contacts. We'll reconvene after the replay results.

[07:59] Maya: Timeline for reconvene? We want quick cadence.

[08:03] Alex: How about end of next week — 2026-02-26? If Priya needs more time for the replay, we'll adjust.

[08:10] Priya: I think 2 business days is enough to get an initial replay and smoke results, but for thorough benching we'll need 4-5 days. We'll aim to share preliminary numbers by 2026-02-23.

[08:20] Jordan: Works for us.

[08:25] Samir: One last item — mention of competitor validation in the exec note. We ran a quick comparison with ModelCorp last month and saw similar tail patterns with mixed tenancy. We should note that in risks.

[08:37] Alex: Noted. We'll keep the exec note short and factual.

[08:40] Maya: Thanks team. Quick recap of ask from us: provide redacted traces, confirm security contacts, and we want the initial replay results.

[08:49] Alex: Correct. I'll email the timeline doc and attach the playbook. Priya will drop the script in the shared folder.

[08:55] Jordan: Expect the trace bundle tonight.

[09:00] Alex: Great. Any final questions?

[09:04] Maya: No, that's it. Thanks.

[09:06] Alex: Thanks all, we'll follow up with the notes and owners.

[09:10] [Meeting ends]

Notes on transcription: occasional ASR mistakes ("K-V cash" for KV cache), some speaker overlaps condensed, timestamps approximate.
